content.introduction: Meta strongly opposes Australia's proposed 2.25% levy on its revenue for sharing news content, calling it unfair and poorly designed. The levy aims to force tech giants to negotiate with local news publishers. Meta argues the law will harm the news industry.
body: # Meta slams Australia’s bid to make tech giants pay for sharing news articles. Meta faces a compulsory levy that will amount to 2.25% of their Australian revenue. Tech giant Meta has attacked Australia’s “grossly unfair” bid to make social media companies pay for news, saying it is vehemently opposed to the draft laws. and Instagram, said in a statement: “Our position is clear: this law is poorly designed, grossly unfair, and will fail to deliver a diverse and sustainable news industry. Social media companies including Meta, Google and TikTok will first be given a chance to strike content deals with local news publishers. If they refuse, they face a compulsory levy that will amount to 2.25% of their Australian revenue. When Canberra mooted similar laws in 2024, Meta announced that Australian users would no longer be able to access the “news” tab. Australia’s University of Canberra has found that more than half the country uses social media as a source of news.
Meta condemns Australia's proposed news levy, calls it flawed, unfair tax that violates free trade.
